ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, Figure A is the image of a transverse harmonic wave at time $t=0$, and point $P$ is a particle at its equilibrium position at this moment. Figure B is the vibration image of particle $P$.

1. What is the propagation speed of this wave?
2. After 30 seconds, what is the distance $x$ that the wave has propagated forward?
3. Determine the direction of propagation of this wave.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure A on the left in the figure is the waveform graph of a transverse wave at t=0, with the vertical axis being y/cm and the horizontal axis being x/m. Crests appear near x=0 and near x=0.8 m, and the trough is at about x=0.4 m, so the distance between adjacent crests is 0.8 m. Point P is located at the equilibrium position y=0, and near this point the waveform crosses downward through the equilibrium position as x increases, so the spatial slope at P is ∂y/∂x<0. Figure B on the right is the vibration graph of particle P, with the vertical axis being y/cm and the horizontal axis being t/s; P moves downward from the equilibrium position at t=0, and later at t=0.6 s repeats the same state of crossing downward through the equilibrium position, so the period T=0.6 s, and at t=0, ∂y/∂t<0. Reasoning: From the distance between adjacent crests in Figure A, the wavelength λ=0.8 m is obtained; from Figure B, the vibration period of the particle T=0.6 s is obtained. The wave speed v=λ/T=0.8/0.6=4/3 m/s. The distance the wave propagates forward within 30 s is s=vt=(4/3)×30=40 m. When judging the direction, the spatial slope of point P at t=0 is ∂y/∂x<0, and the direction of vibration velocity corresponds to ∂y/∂t<0; the two have the same sign. For a left-traveling wave y=f(x+vt), there is ∂y/∂t=v∂y/∂x, and the two have the same sign; for a right-traveling wave, the two have opposite signs. Therefore this wave propagates to the left.
